thread:
maya: Hey team — just got a support ticket where the customer says requests with region=us-west are being routed to EU and latency spikes. They pasted a raw request header and I think the SDK might be sending a weird token.

Customer sample:
```
POST /v1/complete
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_XXX
Region: \"us-west\"\n  
Content-Type: application/json
```

maya: note the extra line/space after the header value. customer says their js-sdk versions 0.9.2/0.9.3 both show this.

aj: can you paste the exact curl they used? router ignores unknown region tokens and falls back to nearest available (we default to eu for that org) so whitespace could make region parsing fail.

maya: here is their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_XXX" \
  -H "Region: \"us-west\"\n" \
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```

aj: ah — the header includes an embedded newline inside the header value. That will cause the edge proxy to treat the header as two tokens. Some proxies then drop/ignore the header value and default routing kicks in.

oncall-bot: router-fallback-alert: org=acme-corp route=completion-us fallback_to=eu count=42 window=10m

tim: we've seen this pattern before with older SDKs that accidentally append `"\n` when building headers in certain envs. We should trim header values at the router level anyway. I'll open a gearbox ticket to add a defensive trim + validation.

maya: customer wants repro steps and a mitigation ASAP — can we give them a quick workaround?

aj: short term: tell them to upgrade to js-sdk 0.9.5 which fixes header serialization (v0.9.5 does not inject newline). Also ask them to remove any manual quoting around the region header — it should be just `Region: us-west`.

maya: sent that. customer confirmed they can patch client and saw requests route to us-west now.

tim: created issue INF-7892 and opened PR https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/4571 to add header trimming at the ingress and add a check that region matches allowed set.

aj: will add a small telemetry alert to detect non-ASCII or whitespace-padded region tokens — should catch regressions.

maya: marking as resolved for now but leaving the internal ticket open until router fix is deployed. thanks :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: deploy pipeline: infra-router-trim-header patch queued for canary deploy (job #2281).

maya: follow-up: customer asked if this could cause billing mismatches — aj, can you confirm billing attribution is based on routed region and we've not double-billed?

aj: billing is attributed to the region that actually served the request. I checked logs for their org and only the fallback eu requests were billed during the incident window — we're issuing a credit for the window since they intended us-west. I'll document in the ticket.

maya: great, closing from support side once credit applied.
